The criterion depends on delivered-markup structure: every paragraph must occur once in normal flow and once inside an inert scroll-driven layer. Visible/extracted text and scrolling confirm the letter exists, but they cannot defensibly establish whether a second copy exists in markup or which copy is in ordinary flow versus the driven layer. Therefore the evidence does not settle the criterion.

The observations do not defensibly establish whether a faint speckle overlay exists or whether it is stacked above the film/still frame and below the darkening panel. A zero animation count alone cannot rule out animation implemented via canvas, video, timers, or animated background assets. Because direct visual and layer-order evidence was unavailable, the criterion cannot be resolved as yes or no.

The catalogue presents exactly five products in a single fixed sequence, with no alternate arrangement controls. Its sequence is not explained by price or alphabetical sorting, supporting that it is an editorial order. Therefore criterion R3 is satisfied.

The product page presents specifications as grouped, labelled rows with every figure/value occupying the same second-column position, rather than as running prose or ragged inline figures. This meets the positive table-and-aligned-numeric-column requirement.

The observations establish an in-place accepted quantity update without a page navigation, but the criterion specifically requires direct evidence that totals enter a pending state and that a server-rejected change reverts the quantity with a stated reason. Those decisive rejection and pending-state observations are missing, so the full composite criterion cannot be resolved defensibly.

The discontinued Monitor Mount product page explicitly states that it is no longer sold and names the exact date through which support continues. Both observed variants showed the required note, and the disabled purchase control corroborates that it is not rendered as an ordinary available product.

In a browser reported by the installer as lacking USB camera capability, the installer substitutes a complete support explanation for the capability control, explicitly names Chrome, Edge, and Opera as working desktop browsers, and directs the customer to the Arranger application. The page is not empty and no nonfunctional USB/connect control is shown in the capability section.

The cart directly labels delivery and tax as estimates before the destination is known and explicitly says the exact amount will be shown once the destination is known. The subsequent completed checkout confirms that the labels become final only after address and delivery information are supplied.

The criterion specifically requires observing the visual treatment of an expired warranty. All available camera-grid fixtures showed active warranties, and missing expired-state evidence cannot defensibly be converted into either a pass or a failure.

The missing-page requirement is met, including what happened and what to do next. However, the failed-sign-in message describes credentials that do not match rather than using the required neutral wording “That did not work.” The evaluation rule says to answer no when either required message describes an invalid value, so the composite criterion is not satisfied.

All four required post-letter surfaces—shop, cart, account, and downloads—were directly inspected. Each prioritizes compact transactional or technical information, and none showed a marketing hero, decorative illustration, or generous editorial whitespace. The full add-to-cart flow, including quantity constraint behavior and confirmation, also exposed the populated cart state needed for a defensible evaluation.

Measured colors and bounding boxes establish the required polarity across the composite: the letter and footer are light type on a dark ground, while the shop, cart, and authenticated account surfaces are dark type on a light ground. No observed surface uses the opposite ground.
